error_kinds.description: A failure without a more specific machine-readable binding classification.
The requested operation identifier or numeric code is not part of the ABI operation vocabulary.
The request is valid but the artifact lacks the named descriptor capability.
The same reusable engine was called or retired while one of its host callbacks was active.
The reusable engine cannot admit the requested operation or close while another operation is active.

entry_point.description: The only exported native ABI symbol. It validates the requested ABI and minimum-prefix layout digest before returning the common prefix of a size-tagged function table.

status_codes.description: A pointer, length, struct size, or option value is invalid.
A UTF-8 input slice is invalid.
Engine or request options JSON is invalid.
The requested operation is unknown or one of its required capabilities is not compiled into this artifact.
A Rust panic was caught at the native boundary.
A configured resource limit was exceeded.
The host requested a different native ABI version.
The host requested a different ABI descriptor layout digest.
A host callback could not produce a result. Rendering may continue through a source-backed fallback.
A callback re-entered or retired the same engine.
The supplied engine token is unknown or has already been released.
The reusable engine has an active operation and cannot be closed or concurrently entered under its callback policy.

callbacks.description: A synchronous host text-measurement callback on the invoking operation thread. It receives borrowed pointer records valid only for the callback duration. Any thread that attempts to re-enter or retire the same engine while this callback is active receives reentrant-call. The callback and user_data remain host-owned and must stay valid until the engine is retired and every operation that acquired it before retirement has returned.

function_slots.description: Return the flat bindings-core runtime catalog JSON for this artifact.
Create a reusable engine from size-tagged configuration.

Attempt to close a reusable engine without waiting. A callback-active engine returns reentrant-call; another active operation returns busy and keeps the token valid; quiescent success retires the token and is a callback-context quiescence barrier.
Execute one generic operation request and return owned bytes in the result.

Release the allocation identified by allocation_token and clear the complete record. Moving the complete record transfers ownership. Zero, unknown, stale, and random non-live tokens release nothing and only clear the supplied record. The token is an ownership identity, not an authorization boundary against hostile same-process memory access.

records.description: A size-tagged borrowed byte slice. Null data is valid only with zero length.
A size-tagged owned byte buffer returned only inside MermanNativeResult.
A size-tagged host text-measurement request. All slices are borrowed for the callback duration.

fields.name: text_measurement_protocol_version
fields.ownership: must match the independent text measurement protocol

records.description: A size-tagged host text-measurement result written by the callback.

fields.name: text_measure
fields.ownership: host-owned callback retained until the engine is retired and every operation acquired before retirement has returned

fields.name: text_measure_user_data
fields.ownership: host-owned opaque pointer with the same lifetime as text_measure

records.description: A size-tagged generic operation request. URI is required only for document-analysis operations. Request options are deeply merged over the reusable engine configuration for this operation.

fields.name: uri
fields.ownership: borrowed for the call; empty when not applicable

fields.name: options_json
fields.ownership: borrowed for the call; recursively overrides engine options except runtime_policy, which is constructor-owned

records.description: A zero-initialized size-tagged operation result with an opaque process-lifetime allocation token, borrowed static media type, and two Merman-owned buffers. Every result written by Merman receives a nonzero token, including empty success and failure payloads. Moving the complete record transfers ownership. Failure JSON follows result schema v1 and carries kind plus a nullable capability_id.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.ownership: caller zero-initializes the complete record and sets this field to sizeof(MermanNativeResult)

fields.name: allocation_token
fields.ownership: opaque Merman-owned allocation identity; zero before output, nonzero after every written result, never reused during the process lifetime

fields.name: data
fields.ownership: owned by Merman through allocation_token until result_free

fields.name: metadata_or_error_json
fields.ownership: owned by Merman through allocation_token until result_free; failure JSON schema v1 always includes kind and capability_id, which is non-null only for missing-capability

records.description: A size-tagged native API discovery request.

fields.name: expected_minimum_prefix_layout_digest
fields.ownership: borrowed expected minimum-prefix layout compatibility digest

records.description: A size-tagged ABI function table. The caller supplies buffer capacity in struct_size; Merman writes the common prefix, then reports the producer full size in struct_size. Function slots append in stable code order.

fields.name: struct_size
fields.ownership: caller initializes to buffer capacity; Merman reports the producer full size on output

fields.name: minimum_prefix_layout_digest
fields.ownership: borrowed static minimum-prefix compatibility digest bytes

fields.name: full_descriptor_digest
fields.ownership: borrowed static full descriptor provenance digest bytes

fields.name: capability_catalog_digest
fields.ownership: borrowed static capability catalog provenance digest

ownership_rules.description: Only result.data and result.metadata_or_error_json identified by a live allocation_token are Merman-owned. Callers zero-initialize the complete result and set struct_size before every producing call. Merman assigns a process-lifetime monotonic nonzero token that is never reused. If token issuance is exhausted, the call returns internal-error and leaves the caller's valid zero-initialized result untouched because no conforming result can be written. Moving the complete record transfers ownership. result_free trusts only the token, never buffer pointers; zero, unknown, stale, and random non-live tokens release nothing and only clear the supplied record. Copying a live token is outside the same-process hostile-memory threat boundary. No result buffer may be passed to a host allocator.
Input, media-type, and callback slices are borrowed. Hosts must not retain their pointers after the enclosing call or callback returns.

Engine tokens are opaque u64 values. engine_try_close never waits: callback-active returns reentrant-call, another active operation returns busy with the token still valid, and quiescent success permanently closes admission before retiring the token. A transport reference acquired before successful close cannot enter afterwards. Callback and user_data are immutable constructor-owned state and may be released after successful close.

Host callbacks are synchronous and borrowed for the call. They MUST NOT unwind, throw, propagate SEH, longjmp, or otherwise perform a non-local exit across the ABI boundary. Merman converts returned status values only; it cannot catch foreign exceptions.

A known operation whose backend is absent returns unsupported_operation with kind missing-capability and the canonical capability_id before result allocation. An unknown operation code returns the same status with kind unknown-operation and a null capability_id.
